diagrams.purpose: Application fleet with a distributed cache
diagrams.description: Three API instances share a cache cluster in front of the source database. The cluster may partition keys across cache nodes and replicate selected ownership for availability.

diagrams.purpose: Possible cache locations in a request path
diagrams.description: A client request may pass through a browser cache, CDN, reverse proxy, application, local cache, distributed cache, and database. Real systems select only the layers that solve a measured problem.

diagrams.purpose: Static cache-stampede fallback
diagrams.description: Ten thousand reads see an expired hot key. Without coordination they can create ten thousand database queries; single-flight coordination permits one query while other requests wait for the repopulated result.

diagrams.purpose: Requirement-driven cache fallback
diagrams.description: The application uses the cache when available. When unavailable, it checks whether bounded origin fallback is safe; otherwise it serves permitted stale data, degrades features, or sheds load.

diagrams.purpose: Cache-aside hit and miss paths
diagrams.description: The application checks key user colon 42. A hit returns directly. A miss causes a database read followed by cache population before the response.

diagrams.purpose: Read-through miss handling
diagrams.description: The application makes one cache call. On a miss, the cache abstraction loads from the database, stores the value, and returns it.

diagrams.purpose: Conceptual write-through flow
diagrams.description: The application writes through the cache layer. The layer persists the backing record and updates its cached copy before reporting success.

diagrams.purpose: Conceptual write-behind flow
diagrams.description: The cache acknowledges an application update first, then persists the buffered or batched change to the database later.

diagrams.purpose: Event-driven cache invalidation
diagrams.description: A source-of-truth write produces a change event. An invalidator removes or updates cached copies, while the dashed path calls out that delivery can be delayed, duplicated, or missed.

diagrams.purpose: Index-assisted lookup
diagrams.description: A query searches a sorted email index, obtains the matching row location, and retrieves the users-table row instead of scanning the full table.

diagrams.purpose: Lost update during seat booking
diagrams.description: Two buyers read one available seat, both write zero remaining, and both may believe they booked because their read-modify-write operations were not coordinated.

diagrams.purpose: Leader and follower replication
diagrams.description: Writes reach a leader and changes propagate to two replicas. Reads may be routed to the leader or a replica, with different freshness and load consequences.

diagrams.purpose: Read immediately after an asynchronous write
diagrams.description: A user updates their profile on the leader, then reads from a replica before replication arrives and observes the older value.

diagrams.purpose: Shard routing by range or directory
diagrams.description: A router uses a shard key to choose among three range shards. An optional directory maps a specific customer to a shard and becomes routing metadata that must remain available and correct.

diagrams.purpose: Session guarantee over asynchronously changing replicas
diagrams.description: A username update commits on the leader and reaches one replica before another. The user reads the updated replica, while another copy can temporarily hold the older value.

diagrams.purpose: Operation policy during a regional partition
diagrams.description: Two regions cannot communicate. The design can reject or pause some operations to preserve a stronger guarantee, or accept independently and reconcile divergence later.

diagrams.purpose: Object bytes and application metadata
diagrams.description: A client uses the application API for metadata recorded in a database, transfers object bytes directly to object storage using authorized access, and objects can later feed a CDN or processing system.

diagrams.purpose: Direct multipart upload
diagrams.description: The client starts an upload through the API, which creates a metadata record and returns signed part URLs. The client uploads parts directly, completes through the API, and object creation can trigger processing.

diagrams.purpose: Horizontal application scaling
diagrams.description: Users reach a load balancer, which routes requests across Server A, Server B, and Server C. This adds capacity and instance redundancy, while introducing routing and health-check requirements.

diagrams.lesson: How to Approach a System Design Interview
diagrams.purpose: A reusable System Design interview flow
diagrams.description: Progress from requirements to scale, interfaces and data, a high-level design, critical flows, bottlenecks, a focused deep dive, failures and trade-offs, then a concise summary. The point is to begin with the problem rather than infrastructure components.

diagrams.purpose: Checkout with a short critical path
diagrams.description: Checkout handles payment synchronously, while email, analytics, and receipt work continue through a queue.

diagrams.purpose: A queue feeding an independent worker pool
diagrams.description: API servers publish jobs to a queue, three workers compete for work, and successful work is acknowledged.

diagrams.purpose: Order event fan-out
diagrams.description: One Order event reaches independent email, analytics, and fraud subscriptions.

diagrams.purpose: Offsets in an append-only log
diagrams.description: Four events occupy consecutive positions 100 through 103 in one retained log partition.

diagrams.purpose: Kafka topic and consumer group
diagrams.description: Producers append to three topic partitions; two members of one consumer group divide partition ownership.

diagrams.purpose: One Kafka partition with replicas
diagrams.description: Broker A leads partition zero while Brokers B and C hold replicas.

diagrams.purpose: Retry exhaustion and dead-letter handling
diagrams.description: A consumer retries a failed message a bounded number of times, then isolates it for inspection, remediation, and safe redrive.

diagrams.purpose: Independent reactions to OrderPlaced
diagrams.description: The order service publishes an event; notification, analytics, and fulfillment react independently.

diagrams.purpose: Transactional outbox
diagrams.description: The order and outbox row commit together in one database transaction; a relay later reads the row and publishes the event.

diagrams.purpose: Change Data Capture pipeline
diagrams.description: A CDC connector reads the database change log and publishes records for search, analytics, and warehouse consumers.

diagrams.purpose: A topic split into four partitions
diagrams.description: One topic distributes records across four independent ordered partitions.

diagrams.purpose: Static two-consumer assignment
diagrams.description: Consumer A owns partitions zero and one, while Consumer B owns partitions two and three.

diagrams.purpose: Side effect succeeds before acknowledgement fails
diagrams.description: The consumer writes the database, crashes before acknowledging, then receives the message again and risks a duplicate write.

diagrams.purpose: Retry after an uncertain payment response
diagrams.description: The first payment succeeds but its response is lost. The client retries with the same key, the API finds the stored outcome, and returns it without creating another payment.

diagrams.purpose: Routing between WebSocket gateways
diagrams.description: Client A sends through Gateway A to a message bus, which delivers to Gateway B and Client B. Both gateways update a connection registry so the system can locate users across servers.

diagrams.purpose: Forward and reverse proxy positions
diagrams.description: Clients use a forward proxy to reach the internet. Internet traffic reaches a reverse proxy, which routes to backend Server A or Server B.

diagrams.purpose: CDN cache hit and miss
diagrams.description: A client requests an object from a nearby edge. A hit returns immediately. On a miss, the edge fetches from the origin, caches according to policy, and returns the object.

diagrams.purpose: Traffic distributed across healthy servers
diagrams.description: Users reach one load-balancing layer, which performs health checks and routes traffic across Server A, Server B, and Server C.

diagrams.purpose: API gateway routing across services
diagrams.description: Clients reach an API gateway, which routes application requests to user, payment, or notification services.

diagrams.purpose: Service registration and lookup
diagrams.description: Three Service B instances register health with a service registry. Service A looks up logical Service B and sends a request to a healthy instance.

diagrams.purpose: Shared state for a distributed limit
diagrams.description: A client reaches three API servers through a load balancer. Each server consults shared limiter state so the same identity is counted across replicas.

diagrams.lesson: How a Request Travels Through a System
diagrams.purpose: An intentionally simplified request path
diagrams.description: A browser resolves DNS and reaches a CDN or edge. A cache hit returns there; a miss continues through a load balancer and API server, which may use Redis or a database. Real systems vary, and not every request visits every component.

diagrams.purpose: Simplified DNS resolution
diagrams.description: A browser asks a recursive resolver. On a cache miss, that resolver consults authoritative DNS, returns an address or endpoint, and may cache the answer for its remaining TTL.

diagrams.purpose: Authorization code flow with PKCE
diagrams.description: A client sends a user to an authorization server with state and a PKCE challenge. The client validates the returned state, exchanges the authorization code with the verifier, and sends the resulting access token only to the intended resource server.

diagrams.purpose: Trace context across an order request
diagrams.description: A client request enters an API and passes trace context through order and payment services. Each service records a child span, so the final trace shows the ordered call path and where latency accumulated.

diagrams.purpose: TLS termination creates an explicit trust boundary
diagrams.description: A client authenticates a TLS endpoint before sending encrypted application data. After termination, the platform starts a separately protected internal connection to the application service, making both hops and the plaintext boundary explicit.

diagrams.purpose: Layer abuse controls before scarce work
diagrams.description: Client traffic passes through edge validation, identity and quota checks, application authorization, and a bounded work queue before reaching a protected dependency. Each layer emits abuse telemetry so operators can distinguish blocked traffic from user-visible failures.

diagrams.purpose: Simplified primary-to-replica failover
diagrams.description: A primary replicates to a replica, becomes unreachable, and a controller promotes the replica before redirecting clients.

diagrams.purpose: Leader replacement with a newer term
diagrams.description: Nodes B and C cannot reach leader A; B wins an election in a newer term, making A's previous term stale.

diagrams.purpose: Two five-node majorities overlap
diagrams.description: One majority includes nodes 1, 2, and 3; another includes 3, 4, and 5; node 3 overlaps.

diagrams.purpose: Proposals become an agreed ordered log
diagrams.description: Three nodes participate in turning a proposed decision into one agreed log.

diagrams.purpose: Raft log replication at interview depth
diagrams.description: A client sends a command to a leader, which replicates the log entry to followers and commits after a majority stores it.

diagrams.purpose: One slow dependency can spread failure upstream
diagrams.description: A client reaches an API, Service A, Service B, and a database; Service B is slow or unreachable.

diagrams.purpose: Retries with increasing randomized waits
diagrams.description: A request fails twice, waits longer with jitter after each failure, and succeeds on its third attempt.

diagrams.purpose: Circuit breaker state transitions
diagrams.description: Closed opens after excessive failures, later probes in half-open, and either closes on success or opens again on failure.

diagrams.purpose: Independent workload pools
diagrams.description: Payment, media, and notification jobs use separate pools; media saturation does not consume payment capacity.

diagrams.purpose: Two-phase commit happy path
diagrams.description: A coordinator asks two databases to prepare; after both vote yes, it tells both to commit.

diagrams.purpose: Orchestrated order Saga with compensation
diagrams.description: An order saga reserves inventory, captures payment, and arranges shipping; payment failure releases inventory.

diagrams.purpose: Two-region architecture baseline
diagrams.description: Global routing sends traffic to APIs in Regions A and B, whose databases replicate between regions.

diagrams.purpose: Active-passive regions
diagrams.description: Users use active Region A; state replicates to standby Region B, which is a failover target.

diagrams.purpose: Active-active regions
diagrams.description: Americas and Europe users use local regions, which replicate with an explicit conflict policy.

diagrams.purpose: Replication and backup protect different failures
diagrams.description: Production data feeds replicated state for availability and point-in-time backups for restoration after deletion or corruption.

diagrams.purpose: Dependencies for a partial-failure review
diagrams.description: An API depends independently on a cache, database, recommendation service, and message broker.

diagrams.purpose: Embedding generation and vector retrieval paths
diagrams.description: Documents and queries pass through an embedding model; the query searches a vector index, producing candidates for optional reranking.

diagrams.purpose: Versioned re-embedding and index replacement
diagrams.description: Documents are embedded into a model-v17 index; model v18 triggers a re-embedding pipeline and a new index used by online queries.

diagrams.purpose: Online and asynchronous model serving
diagrams.description: Online requests are load balanced across versioned inference servers using compute accelerators, while asynchronous jobs use a queue and batch workers.

diagrams.purpose: Feature pipeline feeding offline and online stores
diagrams.description: Raw data enters a feature pipeline that writes historical offline features for training and current online features for inference.

diagrams.purpose: Collaborative editing service and durable operation history
diagrams.description: Two clients maintain persistent connections to a collaboration service backed by an operation or document log and snapshots.

diagrams.purpose: Conceptual OT coordination
diagrams.description: Two clients send concurrent inserts to a collaboration server, which orders and transforms them before returning adjusted operations.

diagrams.purpose: Multi-channel notification delivery
diagrams.description: A product event passes through preference and template selection into separate push, email, and SMS workers that record delivery results.

diagrams.purpose: Schedule storage separated from execution
diagrams.description: A scheduler finds due jobs in a database and dispatches them to a ready queue consumed by workers.

diagrams.purpose: Crawler frontier, fetch, parse, and deduplicate loop
diagrams.description: Seeds enter a URL frontier; workers fetch and parse pages; documents are stored and newly extracted URLs pass through deduplication back into the frontier.

diagrams.purpose: Video upload processing fan-out
diagrams.description: An uploaded object emits an event that independently triggers transcoding, thumbnails, and moderation; renditions are published behind a CDN.

diagrams.purpose: Conceptual full-text search pipeline
diagrams.description: Documents are analyzed into an inverted index; a query retrieves candidate documents that are ranked into results.

diagrams.purpose: Search as a derived read model
diagrams.description: Writes commit to the primary database and later flow through CDC or an outbox to the search index; searches read the index.

diagrams.purpose: Distributed search fan-out and merge
diagrams.description: A coordinating search node fans a query to three shards and merges their ranked responses.

diagrams.purpose: Offline aggregation feeding online autocomplete
diagrams.description: Query logs are aggregated into a popular-prefix dataset, loaded into an autocomplete store, and served through a low-latency API and cache.

diagrams.purpose: Adaptive four-way spatial partitioning
diagrams.description: A large region splits into four quadrants; only the dense northeast quadrant splits again.

diagrams.purpose: Clients coordinate through a small hierarchical namespace
diagrams.description: Scheduler, worker, and service clients use a ZooKeeper ensemble containing persistent configuration, an ephemeral service registration, and an election candidate node; clients observe relevant watch events.

diagrams.purpose: Raft-replicated metadata with watches and leases
diagrams.description: Controllers send requests through an etcd leader replicated to two followers. The versioned key-value state feeds watch streams and may bind keys to expiring leases.

diagrams.purpose: Stateful stream-processing pipeline
diagrams.description: An event source feeds Flink operators that read and update keyed state, emit to downstream systems, and periodically store checkpoints in durable storage.

diagrams.purpose: Shared low-latency state with an explicit durable boundary
diagrams.description: Application servers use a Redis cluster for shared fast state and a durable database where the workload requires an authoritative source. A Redis primary shard replicates to replicas.

diagrams.purpose: Retained partitions serving independent consumer groups
diagrams.description: Producers write to a Kafka broker cluster containing three topic partitions. Two independent consumer groups each track their own progress across those partitions.

diagrams.purpose: Partition leader and replicas
diagrams.description: A producer writes to a partition leader, which replicates records to followers before consumers read the retained log according to configuration.

diagrams.purpose: PostgreSQL primary with streaming standbys
diagrams.description: Application writes and correctness-sensitive reads go to the primary; write-ahead log records stream to two standbys that may serve staleness-tolerant reads.

diagrams.purpose: Access patterns become partitioned key paths
diagrams.description: An application access pattern selects a partition key distributed across storage partitions, while a secondary access pattern uses an independently partitioned global secondary index.

diagrams.purpose: Authoritative writes feeding a derived search index
diagrams.description: A primary database emits changes through CDC or an outbox into an event stream; an indexer updates the search cluster, which serves ranked queries.

diagrams.purpose: Authorized direct upload and event-driven processing
diagrams.description: A client requests upload authorization from an API, records pending metadata, uploads directly to object storage, and a worker consumes an object event before marking the item ready.

diagrams.purpose: A coordinator routes one partition to its replicas
diagrams.description: A client contacts a coordinator, which hashes the partition key to a token and sends work to three replicas before satisfying the selected consistency level.

diagrams.purpose: RabbitMQ exchange routing
diagrams.description: A producer publishes to an exchange whose bindings and routing keys direct messages to two queues, each served by its own consumers.

diagrams.purpose: Receive, process, delete—or become visible again
diagrams.description: A consumer receives a queued message, making it temporarily invisible. Success deletes it; a crash lets the visibility timeout expire so it may be delivered again.
